19: /// Responsible for registering wakeups when an OS signal is received, and
20: /// subsequently dispatching notifications to any signal listeners as appropriate.
21: ///
22: /// Note: this driver relies on having an enabled IO driver in order to listen to
23: /// pipe write wakeups.
24: #[derive(Debug)]
25: pub(crate) struct Driver {
26:     /// Thread parker. The `Driver` park implementation delegates to this.
27:     park: IoDriver,
28: 
29:     /// A pipe for receiving wake events from the signal handler
30:     receiver: PollEvented<UnixStream>,
31: 
32:     /// Shared state
33:     inner: Arc<Inner>,
34: }

44: // ===== impl Driver =====

46: impl Driver {
47:     /// Creates a new signal `Driver` instance that delegates wakeups to `park`.
48:     pub(crate) fn new(park: IoDriver) -> io::Result<Self> {
49:         use std::mem::ManuallyDrop;
50:         use std::os::unix::io::{AsRawFd, FromRawFd};
51: 
52:         // NB: We give each driver a "fresh" receiver file descriptor to avoid
53:         // the issues described in alexcrichton/tokio-process#42.
54:         //
55:         // In the past we would reuse the actual receiver file descriptor and
56:         // swallow any errors around double registration of the same descriptor.
57:         // I'm not sure if the second (failed) registration simply doesn't end
58:         // up receiving wake up notifications, or there could be some race
59:         // condition when consuming readiness events, but having distinct
60:         // descriptors for distinct PollEvented instances appears to mitigate
61:         // this.
62:         //
63:         // Unfortunately we cannot just use a single global PollEvented instance
64:         // either, since we can't compare Handles or assume they will always
65:         // point to the exact same reactor.
66:         //
67:         // Mio 0.7 removed `try_clone()` as an API due to unexpected behavior
68:         // with registering dups with the same reactor. In this case, duping is
69:         // safe as each dup is registered with separate reactors **and** we
70:         // only expect at least one dup to receive the notification.
71: 
72:         // Manually drop as we don't actually own this instance of UnixStream.
73:         let receiver_fd = globals().receiver.as_raw_fd();
74: 
75:         // safety: there is nothing unsafe about this, but the `from_raw_fd` fn is marked as unsafe.
76:         let original =
77:             ManuallyDrop::new(unsafe { std::os::unix::net::UnixStream::from_raw_fd(receiver_fd) });
78:         let receiver = UnixStream::from_std(original.try_clone()?);
79:         let receiver = PollEvented::new_with_interest_and_handle(
80:             receiver,
81:             Interest::READABLE | Interest::WRITABLE,
82:             park.handle(),
83:         )?;
84: 
85:         Ok(Self {
86:             park,
87:             receiver,
88:             inner: Arc::new(Inner(())),
89:         })

92:     /// Returns a handle to this event loop which can be sent across threads
93:     /// and can be used as a proxy to the event loop itself.

95:         Handle {
96:             inner: Arc::downgrade(&self.inner),
97:         }
98:     }

100:     fn process(&self) {
101:         // Check if the pipe is ready to read and therefore has "woken" us up
102:         //
103:         // To do so, we will `poll_read_ready` with a noop waker, since we don't
104:         // need to actually be notified when read ready...
105:         let waker = unsafe { Waker::from_raw(RawWaker::new(ptr::null(), &NOOP_WAKER_VTABLE)) };
106:         let mut cx = Context::from_waker(&waker);
107: 
108:         let registration = self.receiver.registration();
109:         let io_handle = registration.handle();
110:         let shared = registration.shared();
111: 
112:         let ev = match registration.poll_read_ready(&mut cx) {
113:             Poll::Ready(Ok(ev)) => ev,
114:             Poll::Ready(Err(e)) => panic!("reactor gone: {}", e),
115:             Poll::Pending => return, // No wake has arrived, bail
116:         };
117: 
118:         let ready = ev.ready;
119:         let tick = ev.tick;
120: 
121:         // Drain the pipe completely so we can receive a new readiness event
122:         // if another signal has come in.
123:         if !ready.is_empty() {
124:             let mut buf = [0; 128];
125:             loop {
126:                 match (&*self.receiver).read(&mut buf) {
127:                     Ok(0) => panic!("EOF on self-pipe"),
128:                     Ok(_) => continue, // Keep reading
129:                     Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => break,
130:                     Err(e) => panic!("Bad read on self-pipe: {}", e),
131:                 }
132:             }
133:         }
134: 
135:         shared.clear_readiness(ReadyEvent { tick, ready });
136: 
137:         globals().storage().for_each(|event_info| {
138:             if !event_info.pending.swap(false, Ordering::SeqCst) {
139:                 return;
140:             }
141: 
142:             // Ignore errors if there are no listeners
143:             let _ = event_info.tx.send(());
144:         });
145: 
146:         // Keep the I/O driver alive for the duration of drain and dispatch.
147:         drop(io_handle);
148:     }
149: }
